classes.objetivo: Reconocer recursos diplomáticos (I'm afraid, perhaps, slightly, I tend to) y ordenarlos según su grado de firmeza al discrepar.

ensenanza.en: I'm afraid I can't agree with the plan as it stands, but perhaps we could look at another option before we decide.
ensenanza.es: Me temo que no puedo estar de acuerdo con el plan tal como está, pero quizá podríamos mirar otra opción antes de decidir.
ensenanza.nota: I'm afraid + oración abre un desacuerdo sin atacar (no lleva of); perhaps + could convierte una orden en propuesta.

ensenanza.en: With all due respect, the date is slightly too early for most of the team, and the budget seems rather optimistic.
ensenanza.es: Con todo respeto, la fecha es algo temprana para la mayor parte del equipo, y el presupuesto parece bastante optimista.
ensenanza.nota: with all due respect precede a una crítica firme; slightly y rather suavizan: «algo» y «bastante».

ensenanza.en: I appreciate the effort behind your proposal, but I suppose the cost is a problem, so I suggest we ask the members first.
ensenanza.es: Agradezco el esfuerzo que hay detrás de tu propuesta, pero supongo que el costo es un problema, así que sugiero que preguntemos primero a los socios.
ensenanza.nota: I appreciate reconoce lo bueno; I suppose suaviza la afirmación; suggest propone en lugar de ordenar.

ensenanza.en: Frankly, I tend to think that a shorter trip would be safer, although I may be wrong about the weather.
ensenanza.es: Sinceramente, tiendo a pensar que un viaje más corto sería más seguro, aunque puede que me equivoque con el clima.
ensenanza.nota: frankly abre con franqueza y tend to suaviza la opinión; may be wrong deja una puerta abierta.

ensenanza.en: A tactful colleague rarely says that you are wrong; she says instead that she sees the matter rather differently.
ensenanza.es: Un colega con tacto rara vez dice que te equivocas; dice, en cambio, que ve el asunto de forma bastante distinta.
ensenanza.nota: tactful no significa ambiguo: se sigue diciendo lo que se piensa, pero sin atacar a la persona.

ensenanza.en: I wonder whether the date is fixed, because I suggest we ask everyone before we commit to anything.
ensenanza.es: Me pregunto si la fecha ya está fijada, porque sugiero que preguntemos a todos antes de comprometernos a nada.
ensenanza.nota: I wonder whether + oración convierte un desacuerdo en una pregunta abierta; suggest, en una propuesta.

explicacion.titulo: La escala de firmeza al discrepar
explicacion.texto: Discrepar con tacto no es hablar sin claridad: es elegir cuánta fuerza das a tu mensaje. Piensa en una escala: brusco («You are wrong»), directo («I don't agree»), suavizado («I'm afraid I don't quite agree») y muy diplomático («I wonder whether we could look at it differently»). Los recursos son aperturas (I appreciate…, with all due respect), suavizantes (slightly, rather), verbos de opinión (I tend to think, I suppose) y preguntas o sugerencias. Suavizar no es esconder tu opinión.

formula.texto: I'm afraid I see it slightly differently.
Perhaps we could try another option.

filas.texto: I'm afraid I don't quite agree.
I wonder whether we could look at it differently.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I'm afraid of we can't finish by Friday.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I'm afraid we can't finish by Friday.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Delante de una oración, I'm afraid va solo: no lleva of.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I am not agree with you, frankly.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Frankly, I don't agree with you.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Agree es un verbo: se niega con don't, no con am not (calco de «no estoy de acuerdo»).

situacion.contexto: Leo y Mia eligen el destino de la excursión de fin de curso.

dialogo.texto: I think we should go to the museum.
dialogo.traduccion: Creo que deberíamos ir al museo.

dialogo.texto: I appreciate the idea, but I'm afraid it is slightly far for a school trip.
dialogo.traduccion: Agradezco la idea, pero me temo que está algo lejos para una excursión escolar.

dialogo.texto: Really? I suppose you are right about the bus.
dialogo.traduccion: ¿De verdad? Supongo que tienes razón con el autobús.

dialogo.texto: Perhaps we could visit the park instead, and I wonder whether everyone would like that.
dialogo.traduccion: Quizá podríamos visitar el parque, y me pregunto si a todos les gustaría.

item.consigna: ¿Qué propone Leo en lugar del museo?

opciones.es: Visitar el parque, si a todos les parece bien.
Ir al museo otro día, cuando haya más tiempo.
Preguntar a todos si quieren ir al museo.

item.feedback: Leo dice: «Perhaps we could visit the park instead, and I wonder whether everyone would like that»: propone el parque.

guiada.consigna: Elige la formulación más diplomática para rechazar la fecha propuesta.
guiada.texto: A colleague proposes holding the review meeting on Monday at eight. You cannot attend, but you want to keep the tone friendly and offer another option.
opciones: I'm afraid Monday at eight is slightly difficult for me; perhaps we could try later?
Monday at eight is impossible for me, so please choose another day.
I don't think Monday at eight works, so we have to change the date.
guiada.feedback: I'm afraid, slightly y perhaps suavizan el rechazo y ofrecen una salida; las otras dos son más directas y no proponen nada.
guiada.pista: Busca la que suma un suavizante y una propuesta en lugar de una orden.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Me temo que no puedo venir el viernes.»
guiada.texto: Thank you very much for the invitation. I'm ___ I cannot come on Friday, but I would love to meet you another day.
guiada.feedback: I'm afraid abre un desacuerdo o un rechazo con tacto.
guiada.pista: Es el adjetivo con el que se abre una negativa amable.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Quizá podríamos mirar otra opción antes de decidir.»
guiada.respuesta: Perhaps we could look at another option before we decide
guiada.feedback: Perhaps + could convierte la idea en una propuesta suave; before we decide marca el momento.
guiada.pista: Empieza con el adverbio que significa «quizá».

practica.consigna: Une cada formulación con su grado de firmeza.
pares: I'm afraid I see it slightly differently.
I wonder whether there might be another way to look at it.
practica.feedback: La firmeza baja cuando se añaden I'm afraid o slightly, y más aún con una pregunta con I wonder whether.

practica.consigna: Escucha el relato de la reunión y elige qué propone Sara.
practica.audio: At the end of the meeting, the chair asked whether anyone wanted to add anything. Sara said that she appreciated the work behind the proposal, and that she was afraid she saw one difficulty. The budget seemed rather optimistic, and she wondered whether the team could test the idea on a smaller scale first. Then Tom, who tends to be blunt, said simply that the plan would not work. Nobody spoke for a moment, and the chair thanked Sara for her suggestion.
opciones: Testing the idea on a smaller scale before committing.
Rejecting the proposal because the budget is too high.
Dropping the plan because Tom thinks it will not work.
practica.feedback: Sara sugiere probar la idea a menor escala; dice que el presupuesto parece optimista, pero no rechaza la propuesta.

practica.consigna: Completa cada frase con el recurso diplomático que encaja.
frases: I ___ we ask everyone before we commit to anything.
The deadline is ___ tight for a project of this size.
___ we could meet again on Thursday to discuss it?
practica.feedback: Suggest propone, rather suaviza el adjetivo tight y Perhaps + could introduce una alternativa.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué da a entender Sara con su pregunta sobre el equipo?
evaluacion.texto: Dear Tom, thank you for your proposal. With all due respect, I'm not entirely convinced that the timetable is realistic, and I wonder whether the team has had enough time to check the figures. Perhaps we could discuss it on Thursday? Best wishes, Sara.
opciones: That she thinks the team has probably not had enough time.
That she has no opinion and only wants some information.
That she will accept the timetable once the figures are checked.
That she would prefer a different team to check the figures.
evaluacion.feedback: I wonder whether es una pregunta suavizada: Sara sugiere, sin afirmarlo, que el equipo no ha tenido tiempo suficiente.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa cada espacio con el recurso que reconoce, suaviza o abre con franqueza.
evaluacion.texto: Pistas en español: valorar, soler, sinceramente.
frases: I ___ your offer, but I'm afraid the price is too high for us.
I ___ to think that a shorter trip would be safer for the group.
___, I think the plan needs more time before we approve it.
evaluacion.feedback: Appreciate reconoce, tend to suaviza la opinión y Frankly abre con franqueza.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el relato y elige qué grado de firmeza muestra Carlos.
evaluacion.audio: Carlos answered the proposal after a long pause. He said that he appreciated the idea and that it was certainly interesting. Then he added that he would need some time to think, and that the date might be difficult. He did not say no, but he did not say yes either, and he avoided looking at Mia.
opciones: Soft: he leaves room but shows a real doubt.
Warm: he fully supports the idea and only needs time to organise it.
Blunt: he rejects the idea openly, though without raising his voice.
evaluacion.feedback: Elogia la idea pero añade que la fecha podría ser difícil y que necesita tiempo: suaviza el mensaje sin ocultar su duda.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «Con todo respeto, me temo que veo la situación de forma bastante distinta.»
evaluacion.respuesta: With all due respect I'm afraid I see the situation rather differently
aceptadas: I'm afraid with all due respect I see the situation rather differently
evaluacion.feedback: With all due respect e I'm afraid se acumulan antes de la posición, y rather suaviza differently.

repaso.consigna: ¿Con qué propósito escribe Sara este mensaje a Tom?
repaso.texto: Thank you for the draft, Tom. I appreciate how much work you put into it, and I'm afraid the ending seems slightly abrupt to me. Perhaps we could add a short paragraph? I would be glad to help with that.
opciones: To ask for a change while keeping a friendly tone.
To reject the draft firmly and ask Tom to start again.
To thank Tom for the draft and tell him it needs no changes.
To warn Tom that the draft is late and must be finished at once.
repaso.feedback: Reconoce el trabajo y suaviza la crítica (slightly abrupt) para pedir un cambio y ofrecer su ayuda.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Me pregunto si podríamos hablar de otra fecha la semana próxima.»
repaso.respuesta: I wonder whether we could talk about another date next week
repaso.feedback: I wonder whether convierte un desacuerdo en una pregunta abierta sobre una alternativa.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «No estoy del todo convencido de que funcione tal como está.»
repaso.texto: I would not call the plan a failure, but I am not ___ convinced that it will work in its present form.
repaso.feedback: Not entirely convinced expresa duda sin rechazar el plan: un desacuerdo parcial y cortés.

classes.objetivo: Matizar un desacuerdo con distancia y concesión: seem y appear, might, somewhat, arguably, preguntas indirectas con whether y los conectores albeit y notwithstanding.

ensenanza.en: The plan seems somewhat expensive for a small club, although it would seem that the members are willing to pay more.
ensenanza.es: El plan parece algo caro para un club pequeño, aunque parecería que los socios están dispuestos a pagar más.
ensenanza.nota: seem + adjetivo presenta una impresión; somewhat baja la fuerza; it would seem that toma aún más distancia.

ensenanza.en: Some members appear to have a different view, and the committee might possibly need more time than it has.
ensenanza.es: Algunos socios parecen tener una opinión distinta, y el comité quizá necesite más tiempo del que tiene.
ensenanza.nota: appear to + verbo describe cómo parece algo; might + possibly acumula dos suavizantes de posibilidad.

ensenanza.en: That is arguably the safest option, albeit not the cheapest, and to a certain extent it reflects what members asked for.
ensenanza.es: Esa es posiblemente la opción más segura, aunque no la más barata, y hasta cierto punto refleja lo que pidieron los socios.
ensenanza.nota: albeit + grupo breve: concesión corta; to a certain extent limita el alcance de lo que afirmas.

ensenanza.en: Notwithstanding the cost, I think the trip is worth it, although it could be argued that a cheaper venue would do just as well.
ensenanza.es: A pesar del costo, creo que el viaje vale la pena, aunque se podría argumentar que un lugar más barato serviría igual de bien.
ensenanza.nota: notwithstanding + nombre reconoce un punto contrario; it could be argued that presenta una objeción sin hacerla tuya.

ensenanza.en: Could you tell me whether the budget is already fixed, or whether the committee is still looking at other options?
ensenanza.es: ¿Podrías decirme si el presupuesto ya está fijado, o si el comité todavía está estudiando otras opciones?
ensenanza.nota: Pregunta indirecta: whether + orden de afirmación, sin inversión del auxiliar.

ensenanza.en: Hedging does not mean avoiding the point: a careful verb and an adverb such as somewhat let you say what you think without closing the conversation.
ensenanza.es: Matizar no es esquivar el asunto: un verbo prudente y un adverbio como «algo» permiten decir lo que piensas sin cerrar la conversación.
ensenanza.nota: El objetivo de matizar es que la otra persona pueda seguir hablando contigo, no borrar tu opinión.

explicacion.texto: Para discrepar sin chocar puedes tomar distancia de lo que dices. Seem y appear (It seems that…, X appears to…) presentan tu opinión como una impresión, no como un hecho; it would seem that toma aún más distancia. Los modales (might, could) y adverbios como arguably, somewhat o possibly restan firmeza. Las preguntas indirectas (Could you tell me whether…?) suenan más corteses y usan orden de afirmación. Albeit (+ adjetivo o grupo breve) y notwithstanding (+ nombre) reconocen un punto contrario sin romper tu argumento.

formula.nota: distancia: una impresión, no un hecho

filas.texto: Could you tell me whether it is ready?

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Could you tell me where is the budget?
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Could you tell me where the budget is?
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En la pregunta indirecta el orden es el de una afirmación: where the budget is.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The idea is good, albeit it is expensive.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The idea is good, albeit expensive.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Albeit va con un adjetivo o un grupo breve, no con una oración con verbo.

situacion.contexto: Carlos y Sara revisan el plan de un torneo escolar.

dialogo.texto: Could you tell me whether the budget is already fixed?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Podrías decirme si el presupuesto ya está fijado?

dialogo.texto: It appears to be fixed, albeit not finished. The plan is arguably a good one, but it might need more time.
dialogo.traduccion: Parece estar fijado, aunque no terminado. El plan es posiblemente bueno, pero podría necesitar más tiempo.

dialogo.texto: Notwithstanding the cost, I think it is worth it.
dialogo.traduccion: A pesar del costo, creo que vale la pena.

opciones.es: Si el presupuesto ya está decidido.
Si el comité ya ha aprobado el torneo.
Si el presupuesto es suficiente para el torneo.

item.feedback: Sara pregunta «whether the budget is already fixed»: quiere saber si el presupuesto está decidido.

guiada.consigna: Elige la versión con seem que suaviza la frase directa sobre el presupuesto.
guiada.texto: A colleague's plan for the club dinner will cost twice the agreed budget. You want to say so without sounding hostile.
opciones: Your plan seems somewhat expensive compared with our budget.
Your plan is seeming somewhat expensive compared with our budget.
Your plan seems that it is somewhat expensive for our budget.
guiada.feedback: Seem + adjetivo funciona sin más (seems somewhat expensive); seem no se usa en forma continua ni con that + it is después de seems.
guiada.pista: Busca la opción en la que seem va directamente con el adjetivo.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «¿Podrías decirme si el presupuesto está fijado?»
guiada.texto: Could you tell me ___ the budget is already fixed? We need to know before we book the room.
guiada.feedback: Whether introduce una pregunta indirecta con orden de afirmación.
guiada.pista: Es la palabra que introduce una pregunta de sí o no dentro de otra frase.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Algunos socios parecen tener una opinión bastante distinta sobre la fecha.»
guiada.respuesta: Some members appear to have a rather different opinion about the date
guiada.feedback: Appear to + verbo presenta la opinión como una impresión; rather suaviza different.
guiada.pista: El verbo appear va seguido de to + verbo.

practica.consigna: Completa cada frase diplomática con la palabra que encaja.
frases: I am not sure ___ the committee has reached a decision.
The results ___ to suggest a link, albeit a weak one.
The new schedule ___ need some changes before Friday.
practica.feedback: Whether abre una pregunta indirecta, appear to toma distancia y might presenta la posibilidad sin afirmarla.

practica.consigna: Escucha el relato de la reunión y elige qué opina la tesorera del plan.
practica.audio: At the club meeting, the treasurer summarised the proposal for the tournament. The plan, she said, seemed somewhat ambitious, albeit well organised, and it might possibly need more time than the committee had. Notwithstanding the cost, she thought the idea was arguably the club's best in years. She asked whether the sponsors had confirmed their support, and several members appeared to share her doubts. The chair said that he would ask them again on Monday.
opciones: It is promising, but she has doubts about time and support.
It is ambitious, so she wants the club to choose a smaller event.
It is the club's best idea in years, and she has no doubts about it.
practica.feedback: Matiza con seemed somewhat ambitious, might possibly y una pregunta sobre los patrocinadores: valora la idea pero deja ver dudas.

practica.consigna: Une cada recurso con su efecto en español.
pares: se podría argumentar que (objeción sin asumirla)
practica.feedback: Cada recurso quita fuerza o reconoce un punto contrario de una manera distinta.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué pregunta indirecta completa correctamente el correo al hotel?
evaluacion.texto: Dear Sir or Madam, we are booking a room for our yearly meeting next month. Before we confirm the booking, we would like to ask you a question about the equipment, because some of our members will give presentations during the morning session.
opciones: Could you tell me whether the room has a projector?
Could you tell me whether has the room a projector?
Could you tell me does the room have a projector?
evaluacion.feedback: En la pregunta indirecta se usa whether + orden de afirmación: whether the room has a projector.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «La propuesta es un intento serio, aunque no perfecto.»
evaluacion.texto: The proposal is a serious attempt to solve the problem, ___ not a perfect one. I am not sure it is enough, but it is a start.
evaluacion.feedback: Albeit introduce una concesión breve sin verbo conjugado.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el fragmento y elige qué actitud muestran los autores ante sus datos.
evaluacion.audio: The report says that the data seem to point to a link between sleep and memory, albeit a weak one. The authors add that the effect might possibly disappear in larger samples. They stop short of any firm conclusion, and arguably that caution is the most honest part of the whole article.
opciones: Cautious: they present the link as possible, not proven.
Optimistic: they see the link as real and expect larger samples to confirm it.
Dismissive: they treat the link as too weak to be worth mentioning.
evaluacion.feedback: Seem to, weak, might possibly y stop short of una conclusión firme muestran cautela: el vínculo es posible, no demostrado.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «A pesar del costo, parecería que el viaje vale la pena.»
evaluacion.respuesta: Notwithstanding the cost, it would seem that the trip is worth it
aceptadas: It would seem that the trip is worth it notwithstanding the cost
evaluacion.feedback: Notwithstanding + nombre abre la concesión y después viene la posición con it would seem that.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué busca Sara con este mensaje al grupo?
repaso.texto: Dear all, it would appear that the room may be somewhat small for the party, since more guests have replied than we expected. I might be wrong, and perhaps the hotel can offer a larger one. Could someone find out whether that is possible? Thanks, Sara.
opciones: To raise a doubt without blaming anyone and ask for help.
To ask the group to cancel the party because the room is too small.
To blame whoever sent out so many invitations.
To insist that the hotel must give a larger room.
repaso.feedback: Con it would appear, may, might y perhaps plantea un problema posible, no un reproche, y pide que alguien lo compruebe.

repaso.consigna: Suaviza la frase directa con seem o appear y un modal de posibilidad.
repaso.texto: Frase directa: «The schedule is too tight and the team will not finish on time.» Reescríbela con seem o appear y might.
repaso.respuesta: The schedule seems somewhat tight, and the team might not finish on time.
aceptadas: The schedule appears to be rather tight, and the team might not be able to finish on time.
It seems that the schedule is somewhat tight, and that the team might not finish on time.
repaso.feedback: Seem o appear convierten «is too tight» en una impresión, y might suaviza la predicción.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Esta es, según se mire, la mejor opción.»
repaso.texto: Several options were considered during the meeting. This is ___ the best one, although the others have some merits as well.
repaso.feedback: Arguably marca que es una opinión defendible, no un hecho.

classes.objetivo: Interpretar rechazos y dudas corteses en diálogos orales (That might be difficult, I'll think about it) y decidir si la persona acepta, duda o rechaza, citando la frase que lo indica.

ensenanza.en: When Sara says “That might be difficult”, she is trying to decline without causing offence, and most listeners will hear a polite no.
ensenanza.es: Cuando Sara dice «Eso podría ser difícil», intenta rechazar sin ofender, y la mayoría de los oyentes entenderá un no cortés.
ensenanza.nota: «That might be difficult» casi siempre es un no educado: el modal might suaviza la negativa.

ensenanza.en: “I'll think about it” often shows that the speaker is hesitant, and without a date or a reason it is usually a lukewarm response.
ensenanza.es: «Lo pensaré» suele mostrar que quien habla está indeciso, y sin fecha ni motivo suele ser una respuesta tibia.
ensenanza.nota: hesitant: no ha dicho que sí; a lukewarm response carece de entusiasmo y de compromiso concreto.

ensenanza.en: Carlos sounded reluctant to commit to the trip, even though his words were friendly and he promised to call on Friday.
ensenanza.es: Carlos sonó reacio a comprometerse con el viaje, aunque sus palabras eran amables y prometió llamar el viernes.
ensenanza.nota: reluctant: no quiere hacerlo pero no lo dice con palabras; commit to + nombre o -ing.

ensenanza.en: Listen to the tone: a flat voice can turn a friendly sentence into a polite no, and a long pause can say even more.
ensenanza.es: Escucha el tono: una voz plana puede convertir una frase amable en un no cortés, y una pausa larga puede decir aún más.
ensenanza.nota: El tono y las pausas cambian el significado de una frase, aunque las palabras sean amables.

ensenanza.en: Ana took the hint and stopped asking, because Tom had tried twice to stall for time instead of answering.
ensenanza.es: Ana captó la indirecta y dejó de preguntar, porque Tom había intentado dos veces ganar tiempo en lugar de responder.
ensenanza.nota: take the hint: entender lo que alguien insinúa sin decirlo; stall for time: dar largas.

ensenanza.en: A flat refusal is rare in polite conversation, so listeners must interpret what is left unsaid and weigh the evidence in the words.
ensenanza.es: Una negativa rotunda es rara en una conversación cortés, así que quien escucha debe interpretar lo que queda sin decir y sopesar las pistas de las palabras.
ensenanza.nota: interpret: leer entre líneas; la decisión (acepta, duda, rechaza) se apoya en la frase exacta que la indica.

explicacion.texto: Las personas corteses rara vez dicen «no» directamente. Frases como «That might be difficult», «I'll think about it», «Maybe another time» o «That's an interesting idea» suelen ser rechazos o dudas. Para interpretarlas busca señales: ¿hay una hora o un compromiso concreto (acepta)? ¿hay vaguedad, un «but» después de un elogio o ninguna alternativa (rechaza)? ¿hay pausas, cambios de tema o un tono plano (duda)? Decide entre acepta, duda o rechaza y apóyate en la frase exacta que lo indica.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: She said “Maybe another time”, so she will come tomorrow.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: She said “Maybe another time”, so she will not come tomorrow.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: «Maybe another time» sin fecha es un rechazo cortés, no una promesa.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: “I'll think about it” always means yes.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: “I'll think about it” often means the person is not sure.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: «I'll think about it» suele mostrar duda, no un sí seguro.

situacion.contexto: Mia invita a Tom a una fiesta y Tom responde con rodeos.

dialogo.texto: Would you like to come to my party on Saturday?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Te gustaría venir a mi fiesta el sábado?

dialogo.texto: That sounds lovely, but I have a lot to do this weekend.
dialogo.traduccion: Suena genial, pero tengo mucho que hacer este fin de semana.

dialogo.texto: Oh. Could you come for an hour?
I'll think about it. Maybe another time.

opciones.es: Que irá seguro a la fiesta.
Que no ha entendido la invitación.

item.feedback: Tom no da hora ni compromiso: usa «but», «I'll think about it» y «Maybe another time», que juntos suenan a rechazo cortés.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué da a entender la respuesta «Maybe another time» en este intercambio?
guiada.texto: Invitation: “We're all going climbing on Friday. Do you want to join us?” Answer: “That sounds lovely. Maybe another time.” The speaker gives no reason and suggests no date.
opciones: She is politely declining and leaving the door open.
She is accepting, but wants to arrive a little late.
She is hesitant and needs a few days to decide.
guiada.feedback: Sin motivo, fecha ni alternativa, «maybe another time» es un rechazo cortés; no da tiempo para decidir.
guiada.pista: Fíjate en si la respuesta da un día concreto o pide tiempo.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Ana captó la indirecta y dejó de preguntar por la fiesta.»
guiada.texto: Ana took the ___ and stopped asking about the party. Tom had answered every invitation with the same vague excuse.
guiada.feedback: Take the hint significa entender lo que alguien insinúa sin decirlo.
guiada.pista: Es la palabra para una señal indirecta.

guiada.consigna: Escucha y decide si Leo acepta, duda o rechaza.
guiada.audio: Thank you so much for asking, and that is a lovely idea. I'm afraid Saturday is very busy for me, though, and I have nothing else to suggest right now.
opciones: He declines politely, without suggesting another day.
He accepts, but needs a little more time to confirm.
He is hesitant and wants to hear more details.
guiada.feedback: El «but» (though) después del elogio, la agenda ocupada y la falta de alternativa indican un rechazo cortés.
guiada.pista: Busca el contraste después del elogio y si hay alguna alternativa.

practica.consigna: Escucha el relato de las respuestas e indica quién muestra duda.
practica.audio: Five friends were invited to the opening of a new café. Mia replied at once that she would be there at six and would bring the cake. Leo said it sounded lovely but that his week was very full, and that they should meet some other time. Ana answered that she would think about it and let them know. Tom wrote that he was very sorry, but he had to work. Carlos said he would love to come and asked whether he could bring a friend.
opciones: Ana, who promises to decide later.
Leo, who says the week is full.
Tom, who says he is very sorry.
practica.feedback: Ana no acepta ni rechaza: promete pensarlo y avisar más tarde. Leo y Tom dan razones para no ir.

practica.consigna: Escucha el mensaje y elige cómo interpretar la respuesta de la persona.
practica.audio: Hmm, I'll think about it. Let me see how my week goes, and I'll let you know. It's just that I have so much on at the moment, and I hate to promise something I might not be able to do.
opciones: She is hesitant: she has not decided and will reply later.
She accepts, but wants to choose the hour herself.
She declines flatly and closes the subject for good.
practica.feedback: «I'll think about it» y «let me see» muestran duda: no hay respuesta todavía, ni un sí ni un no rotundo.

practica.consigna: Une cada frase cortés con su lectura real.
pares: Count me in; I'll bring the cake.
Let me see how my week goes.
That might be difficult, I'm afraid.
I'd be glad to help, though I can only stay an hour.
practica.feedback: Un compromiso concreto es aceptar, «let me see» es dudar, un modal suavizado rechaza y un límite de tiempo es una condición.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el relato y elige qué quiere decir realmente Sara.
evaluacion.audio: Mia invited Sara to dinner on Saturday. Sara thanked her warmly, said that Saturday might be difficult, and added that she hoped the dinner would go well. She did not mention any other day, and when Mia suggested Sunday instead, she said she would have to see.
opciones: She would rather not come, but avoids saying so.
She will come if Mia moves the dinner to Sunday.
She has another plan for Saturday and feels annoyed.
evaluacion.feedback: «Might be difficult», los buenos deseos finales y el «I'll have to see» ante la alternativa son señales de un rechazo cortés.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Cómo se interpreta la última respuesta de Sara a Leo?
evaluacion.texto: Leo asked Sara to help him move on Sunday. She answered that she would love to, but that she had an exam on Monday and needed the whole weekend to study. Leo asked whether she could come for an hour, and Sara said she would see if she could, but that he should not count on her.
opciones: A polite no: she warns him not to expect her.
An open yes: she promises to come for an hour.
A request for more time so that she can decide.
evaluacion.feedback: «He should not count on her» anula el «I would see»: es un rechazo cortés con una razón, no una promesa ni una petición de tiempo.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el diálogo y decide si Carlos acepta, duda o rechaza.
evaluacion.audio: Ana suggested that they meet on Friday at seven. Carlos answered that Friday at seven was perfect, and he offered to book the table. He also asked whether Ana would like him to invite Tom.
opciones: He accepts and confirms the time.
He declines politely.
He is hesitant about the day.
evaluacion.feedback: Carlos confirma día y hora y se ofrece a reservar: acepta con un compromiso concreto.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Su tono reacio mostraba que no quería ir.»
evaluacion.texto: Carlos said all the right words, but his voice was flat and his answers were short. It was clear from his ___ tone that he did not really want to go.
evaluacion.feedback: Reluctant describe a quien no quiere hacer algo pero no lo dice con palabras.

repaso.consigna: ¿Cómo interpretas la respuesta de Mia a la invitación de Tom?
repaso.texto: Tom asked Mia whether she wanted to see the new film with him and his cousins on Friday. Mia answered that it was an interesting idea and that they would see. She did not ask what time it started, and she changed the subject to her exams.
opciones: She is hesitant and probably does not want to go.
She is keen to go but has not seen the time yet.
She is reluctant only because the cousins will be there.
repaso.feedback: «We'll see», sin preguntar el horario y con cambio de tema, es una respuesta tibia: duda y probablemente no quiere ir.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige cómo termina la respuesta de la persona.
repaso.audio: Thank you for the invitation. I would love to join you, but tomorrow is full, and so is the rest of the week. Perhaps next month, when the project is finished? Please ask me again then.
opciones: She declines for now but leaves the door open.
She accepts for next month and confirms the date.
She declines and does not want to be asked again.
repaso.feedback: Rechaza con «but tomorrow is full» y propone otra fecha con «perhaps next month»: no cierra la puerta.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Quien escucha debe interpretar lo que queda sin decir en un rechazo cortés.»
repaso.respuesta: Listeners must interpret what is left unsaid in a polite refusal
repaso.feedback: Interpret what is left unsaid resume la idea de leer entre líneas un rechazo cortés.

classes.objetivo: Discrepar con tacto en un diálogo: reconocer lo válido, marcar el contraste con although, matizar tu posición y ofrecer una alternativa o un punto medio.

vocabulario.es: ceder ambos, llegar a un punto medio

ensenanza.en: You make a fair point about the price, although I see it differently, and my main concern is the choice of venue.
ensenanza.es: Tienes razón en lo del precio, aunque yo lo veo distinto, y mi principal preocupación es la elección del local.
ensenanza.nota: a fair point reconoce lo razonable antes de discrepar; although marca el contraste sin añadir but.

ensenanza.en: I understand your concern, but instead of cancelling the dinner, we could move it to Sunday.
ensenanza.es: Entiendo tu preocupación, pero en lugar de cancelar la cena, podríamos pasarla al domingo.
ensenanza.nota: concern nombra lo que inquieta al otro; instead of + -ing propone otra acción en lugar de la primera.

ensenanza.en: That is a valid proposal; however, the alternative might be cheaper, and I suspect we will never quite see eye to eye on the cost.
ensenanza.es: Es una propuesta válida; sin embargo, la alternativa podría ser más barata, y sospecho que nunca nos pondremos del todo de acuerdo en el costo.
ensenanza.nota: valid reconoce; however marca el contraste; see eye to eye significa coincidir plenamente.

ensenanza.en: If you want the park and I want a picnic, we could meet halfway and split the difference, which is a fair compromise.
ensenanza.es: Si tú quieres el parque y yo un picnic, podríamos ceder los dos y repartir la diferencia, lo cual es un acuerdo justo.
ensenanza.nota: meet halfway: cada uno cede un poco; split the difference: cada uno asume la mitad de lo que los separa.

ensenanza.en: Sometimes the most honest result is to agree to differ, but a good negotiator first searches for a middle ground and offers an alternative.
ensenanza.es: A veces el resultado más honesto es aceptar que se piensa distinto, pero un buen negociador busca primero un terreno intermedio y ofrece una alternativa.
ensenanza.nota: agree to differ cierra el desacuerdo sin ganador; a middle ground es la posición intermedia que ambos aceptan.

ensenanza.en: My proposal is a compromise that keeps everyone involved, so I suggest we try it for a month and then review it together.
ensenanza.es: Mi propuesta es un acuerdo que mantiene a todos implicados, así que sugiero probarla durante un mes y revisarla juntos.
ensenanza.nota: proposal y compromise cierran el desacuerdo con una salida concreta y revisable.

explicacion.texto: Un desacuerdo bien llevado tiene cuatro pasos: (1) reconoce lo razonable (You make a fair point); (2) marca el contraste con although, while o however y expresa tu posición con matices (I'm not entirely convinced); (3) ofrece una alternativa (How about…? Instead of… we could…); (4) busca un punto medio (Let's meet halfway). Así la otra persona siente que la escuchas y que hay una salida. En español se dice «aunque… pero»; en inglés se usa uno solo: although… sin but.

formula.texto: although I see it slightly differently.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Instead to cancel, we could move it.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Instead of cancelling, we could move it.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Después de instead se usa of + verbo en -ing, no to + verbo.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Although I understand you, but I think it is expensive.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Although I understand you, I think it is expensive.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Although ya marca el contraste: no se añade but (calco de «aunque… pero»).

situacion.contexto: Ana y Leo discrepan sobre dónde celebrar el cumpleaños de Mia.

dialogo.texto: I think we should have the party at a restaurant.
dialogo.traduccion: Creo que deberíamos celebrar la fiesta en un restaurante.

dialogo.texto: You make a fair point about the food, although I'm not entirely convinced about the cost.
dialogo.traduccion: Tienes razón en lo de la comida, aunque no estoy del todo convencido por el costo.

dialogo.texto: Let's meet halfway: we cook at my house, and Mia chooses the cake.
dialogo.traduccion: Busquemos un punto medio: cocinamos en mi casa y Mia elige el pastel.

opciones.es: Cocinar en su casa y dejar que Mia elija el pastel.
Ir al restaurante y repartir el costo entre todos.
Cocinar en casa de Ana y comprar el pastel ya hecho.

item.feedback: Leo dice: «we cook at my house, and Mia chooses the cake»: esa es su propuesta de compromiso.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Tienes razón en lo de la comida, aunque yo lo veo distinto.»
guiada.texto: You make a ___ point about the food, although I see it differently. Still, I am not entirely convinced that a restaurant is the right choice for everyone.
guiada.feedback: Fair point reconoce lo razonable del otro antes de discrepar.
guiada.pista: Es el adjetivo de «a fair point»: razonable, justo.

guiada.consigna: Elige la frase correcta para ofrecer una alternativa a cancelar la cena.
guiada.texto: Your friend wants to cancel the dinner because the restaurant is closed on Monday. You want to keep the plan and suggest a different day.
opciones: Instead of cancelling, we could move the dinner to Tuesday.
Instead to cancel, we could move the dinner to Tuesday.
Instead cancelling, we could move the dinner to Tuesday.
guiada.feedback: Instead se une con of y un verbo en -ing: instead of cancelling.
guiada.pista: Piensa en la preposición que acompaña a instead y en la forma del verbo.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Busquemos un punto medio y repartamos la diferencia entre tu idea y la mía.»
guiada.respuesta: Let's meet halfway and split the difference between your idea and mine
guiada.feedback: Meet halfway y split the difference expresan que cada uno cede un poco.
guiada.pista: Empieza con Let's y termina con el contraste entre dos ideas.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué versión de la respuesta de Leo evita el error de «although… but»?
practica.texto: Leo wants to answer Ana's plan for an expensive dinner politely, and he writes three versions before he sends one of them.
opciones: Although I understand your concern, I think the dinner is too expensive.
Although I understand your concern, but I think the dinner is too expensive.
Although I understand your concern, however I think the dinner is too expensive.
practica.feedback: Although ya marca el contraste: no se añade but, como sí se hace en español con «aunque… pero».

practica.consigna: Escucha el relato y elige qué alternativa propone Mia.
practica.audio: Tom wanted to watch a film tonight, but Mia was tired. She began by telling him that it was a fair point that the film was about to leave the cinema, although she was not sure she could stay awake. Then she suggested that, instead of going tonight, they could go on Saturday afternoon and have dinner afterwards. Tom thought about it for a moment, smiled, and agreed that it was a good compromise, because it gave each of them something and cost neither of them a whole evening.
opciones: Going to the film on Saturday afternoon and eating afterwards.
Watching the film at home tonight and eating out later.
Going tonight, but leaving before the film ends.
practica.feedback: Mia reconoce el punto de Tom y propone «instead of going tonight» ir el sábado por la tarde y cenar después.

practica.consigna: Completa cada paso del desacuerdo con la palabra adecuada.
frases: I understand your ___, but I would like to explain my side.
Let's ___ halfway and choose a day in the middle.
Instead of arguing, we could agree on an ___ plan.
practica.feedback: Concern nombra lo que inquieta, meet halfway busca el punto medio y alternative nombra otra opción.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe un diálogo de ocho turnos en el que dos amigos discrepan con tacto.
evaluacion.texto: Ana y Leo quieren celebrar el fin de curso. Ana prefiere un parque de atracciones y Leo un picnic. Escribe ocho turnos (Ana, Leo, Ana, Leo…) con reconocimiento del punto del otro, concesión, un matiz, una alternativa y un punto medio.
evaluacion.respuesta: Ana: I think we should celebrate the end of term at the theme park, because everyone enjoys the rides and the day would be unforgettable. Leo: You make a fair point about the rides, although I see it slightly differently, and my main concern is the price of the tickets. Ana: I understand your concern, but the park has a group discount, and I suppose that makes it more reasonable than it looks. Leo: That is a valid point, albeit one I cannot check right now. I'm afraid some of our friends cannot afford even a discounted ticket. Ana: Hmm, I had not thought about that. What do you suggest instead? Leo: How about a picnic by the river, with games and music? It would be cheaper, and everyone could come without worrying about money. Ana: A picnic is an alternative I like, although I wonder whether the weather might spoil it. Perhaps we could have both, on different days? Leo: Let's meet halfway: a picnic on Friday afternoon and, if the group has enough money, the park on Saturday. Does that sound fair?
aceptadas: Ana: I would like a big dinner at a restaurant to celebrate the end of term, because the food there is excellent and everybody could sit together. Leo: That is a valid idea, although I am not entirely sure about the cost, and my concern is that some friends might not come. Ana: I understand your concern, but the restaurant offers a fixed price, and I suppose that keeps things under control. Leo: I see your point. However, I wonder whether everyone can pay so much, because a fixed price is still a lot for students. Ana: Perhaps you are right. What do you suggest instead? Leo: How about a dinner at my house? We could cook together, and it would be much cheaper for the whole group. Ana: That sounds fun, although I'm afraid my cooking is not very good. I suppose it is a good compromise, as long as I can choose the dessert. Leo: Great! You choose the dessert, I choose the music, and we split the difference on the cost.
evaluacion.feedback: Un buen diálogo reconoce (fair point), marca el contraste (although), matiza (I'm afraid, slightly), ofrece una alternativa (instead, how about) y cierra con un punto medio.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué hace Tom para discrepar con tacto de la propuesta de Sara?
evaluacion.texto: Sara proposed holding the team meeting on Friday evening. Tom answered that he could see why she wanted to finish the week with a clear plan, but that Friday evening was difficult for most of the team. He wondered whether Monday morning might work instead, and offered to prepare the agenda himself.
opciones: He acknowledges her reason, names a problem and offers an alternative.
He rejects her reason, but agrees to Friday if she prepares the agenda.
He accepts Friday evening, but asks for a shorter meeting instead.
He says nothing about the day and asks her to choose another one.
evaluacion.feedback: Reconoce el motivo de Sara, señala que el viernes por la tarde es difícil y propone el lunes por la mañana, ofreciéndose a preparar la agenda.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Ninguno quiere pagar todo, así que repartamos la diferencia.»
evaluacion.texto: Neither of us wants to pay the full price for the room, so let's split the ___ and each pay half of the extra cost.
evaluacion.feedback: Split the difference es la colocación para que cada parte asuma la mitad de lo que las separa.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «Entiendo tu preocupación, pero quizá podríamos encontrar un punto medio.»
evaluacion.respuesta: I see your concern but perhaps we could find a middle ground
evaluacion.feedback: Concern reconoce la inquietud del otro y perhaps we could introduce la propuesta de un punto medio.

repaso.consigna: Escucha el relato y elige cómo reconoce Sara el punto de su amigo.
repaso.audio: Sara listened to her friend's plan for the trip. She told him that it was a fair point that the train would be quicker, although she was not entirely sure it would suit everyone, because some of the group could not afford the ticket. She did not reject the plan; she asked whether they could look for something cheaper.
opciones: She accepts part of his idea but keeps a doubt.
She rejects his idea in favour of a cheaper one.
She agrees with everything he says about the train.
repaso.feedback: «Fair point» acepta una parte; «not entirely sure» mantiene la duda, y la pregunta final pide una alternativa sin rechazar el plan.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué frase ofrece la contrapropuesta más diplomática?
repaso.texto: Mia wants to hold the party at a restaurant, but Leo thinks it is too expensive for some of the guests. He wants to answer without upsetting her, and still suggest a cheaper place.
opciones: I take your point, but how about a cheaper place instead?
I take your point, but the restaurant is too expensive, so we must choose another.
I am not entirely convinced, so perhaps you should find a cheaper place yourself.
repaso.feedback: Reconocer el punto de Mia y proponer «how about… instead» mantiene la relación; las otras dos dictan la decisión o pasan la carga a Mia.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Tras una hora sin convencernos, acordamos no estar de acuerdo.»
repaso.texto: We talked for an hour without convincing each other, so in the end we decided to agree to ___ and to stay friends.
repaso.feedback: Agree to differ es la expresión para cerrar un desacuerdo sin ganador.

classes.objetivo: Gestionar un desacuerdo entre culturas y reparar un malentendido: nombrar el problema sin culpar, aclarar la intención, disculparse, explicar una costumbre y proponer seguir adelante.

vocabulario.es: suavizar las cosas, allanar el conflicto

vocabulario.en: give the benefit of the doubt
vocabulario.es: conceder el beneficio de la duda

ensenanza.en: I think there was a misunderstanding about my answer, and I would hate you to take it the wrong way.
ensenanza.es: Creo que hubo un malentendido sobre mi respuesta, y no quisiera que lo tomaras a mal.
ensenanza.nota: misunderstanding nombra el problema sin culpar a nadie; take it the wrong way: interpretar mal las palabras o la intención.

ensenanza.en: I did not intend to offend you, and I am sorry that my reply may have come across as rude.
ensenanza.es: No tuve la intención de ofenderte, y lamento que mi respuesta pudiera parecer grosera.
ensenanza.nota: intend to + verbo aclara tu intención; come across as rude describe el efecto que causó, no lo que querías.

ensenanza.en: Let me clarify what I meant, because a short answer like mine can easily give the wrong impression.
ensenanza.es: Déjame aclarar lo que quise decir, porque una respuesta breve como la mía puede dar fácilmente una impresión equivocada.
ensenanza.nota: clarify: explicar de nuevo para que se entienda; give the wrong impression nombra el efecto sin acusar a nadie.

ensenanza.en: In my country it is a custom to refuse an offer twice before accepting it, so my first refusal was not meant seriously.
ensenanza.es: En mi país es costumbre rechazar una oferta dos veces antes de aceptarla, así que mi primera negativa no iba en serio.
ensenanza.nota: custom explica la diferencia cultural sin justificarse; it is a custom to + verbo.

ensenanza.en: I apologise for the confusion, and I hope that a sincere apology will help us to smooth things over.
ensenanza.es: Me disculpo por la confusión, y espero que una disculpa sincera nos ayude a allanar el conflicto.
ensenanza.nota: apologise for + motivo: la disculpa breve; smooth things over: reparar la relación con calma.

ensenanza.en: When a foreign colleague's words seem unfriendly, it is wiser to give the benefit of the doubt and ask them to clarify.
ensenanza.es: Cuando las palabras de un colega extranjero parecen poco amables, es más sensato concederle el beneficio de la duda y pedirle que lo aclare.
ensenanza.nota: give the benefit of the doubt: suponer buena intención antes de juzgar; ask + to clarify pide una aclaración.

explicacion.texto: Cuando personas de culturas distintas chocan, casi siempre hay un malentendido, no mala intención. Para repararlo: (1) nombra el problema sin culpar (I think there was a misunderstanding); (2) aclara tu intención (I did not intend to offend you); (3) reconoce el efecto (I am sorry it came across as rude); (4) explica la costumbre sin justificarte (In my country it is a custom…); (5) propón seguir adelante (Could we start again?). Usa lo aprendido: suavizantes, preguntas indirectas y alternativas.

formula.texto: I think there was a misunderstanding.
I did not intend to offend you,
and I apologise if it sounded rude.

filas.texto: mostrar que no fue a propósito

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I did not intend offend you.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I did not intend to offend you.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Intend va seguido de to + verbo: intend to offend.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I apologise you for the misunderstanding.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Apologise va con for + motivo; si nombras a la persona, se usa to you.

situacion.contexto: Mia, de Ecuador, y Tom, de Escocia, hablan de un malentendido sobre una invitación.

dialogo.texto: I think there was a misunderstanding. When you said maybe, I thought you did not want to come.
dialogo.traduccion: Creo que hubo un malentendido. Cuando dijiste «quizá», pensé que no querías venir.

dialogo.texto: I did not intend to offend you. In my country it is a custom to say maybe when we are not sure.
dialogo.traduccion: No tuve la intención de ofenderte. En mi país es costumbre decir «quizá» cuando no estamos seguros.

dialogo.texto: Thank you for telling me. In my country maybe often means no.
dialogo.traduccion: Gracias por decírmelo. En mi país «quizá» suele significar no.

dialogo.texto: Then let me clarify: I would love to come on Saturday.
dialogo.traduccion: Entonces déjame aclarar: me encantaría ir el sábado.

item.consigna: ¿Por qué hubo un malentendido entre Mia y Tom?

opciones.es: Mia dijo «maybe» por costumbre y Tom lo entendió como un no.
Mia dijo «no» y Tom lo entendió como un quizá.
Tom dijo «maybe» por costumbre y Mia lo entendió como un no.

item.feedback: Mia explica que en su país «maybe» se dice por costumbre cuando no se está seguro; Tom lo leyó como un no.

guiada.consigna: Elige la frase que nombra el problema sin culpar a nadie.
guiada.texto: After the dinner, Mia realises that her words upset Tom. She wants to open the conversation without blaming him or defending herself.
opciones: I think we had a misunderstanding about what I said.
I think you did not understand me, and that is why you are upset.
I apologise, but you should not have taken it so seriously.
guiada.feedback: «A misunderstanding» habla de lo ocurrido entre los dos; las otras frases dejan caer la culpa sobre Tom, de forma directa o disfrazada.
guiada.pista: Busca la que habla de lo ocurrido, no de la persona.

guiada.texto: I did not ___ to offend you. I only wanted to show respect in the way that is usual in my country.
guiada.feedback: I did not intend to… aclara que no fue a propósito.
guiada.pista: Es el verbo que significa «tener la intención de».

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Déjame aclarar lo que quise decir antes de que esto sea un malentendido.»
guiada.respuesta: Let me clarify what I meant before this becomes a misunderstanding
guiada.feedback: Let me clarify abre una aclaración sin culpar al otro; before this becomes… la sitúa a tiempo.
guiada.pista: Empieza con Let me y termina con la palabra que nombra el problema.

practica.consigna: Elige la disculpa correcta por el malentendido y el silencio posterior.
practica.texto: Mia is writing to Tom after the dinner. She wants to apologise for the confusion and also for the days of silence that followed it.
opciones: I apologise for the misunderstanding and for not writing sooner.
I apologise you for the misunderstanding and for not writing sooner.
I apologise of the misunderstanding and for not writing sooner.
practica.feedback: Apologise se une con for + motivo; no lleva complemento directo de persona.

practica.consigna: Escucha el relato y elige qué aclara Ana sobre su costumbre.
practica.audio: Ana, who comes from Ecuador, told her new colleague Luna that in her country it is a custom to say maybe when you want to be polite. She explained that for her, maybe was never a promise or a refusal, only a way of keeping the conversation warm. Luna had taken it as a no, and she was surprised. She thanked Ana for clarifying it, and said that in her own country maybe often does mean no.
opciones: Saying maybe is her polite habit, not a refusal.
She says maybe when she really means no.
She never uses the word maybe with colleagues.
practica.feedback: Ana explica que maybe es una forma cortés de mantener la conversación, no un rechazo ni una promesa.

practica.consigna: Une cada frase de reparación con su función.
pares: I think there was a misunderstanding.
I did not intend to offend you.
aclara que no fue a propósito
I apologise if it came across as rude.
In my country it is a custom to do this.
practica.feedback: Cada frase cumple un paso distinto de la reparación.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe el mensaje de reparación de Mia a Tom (unas 170 palabras).
evaluacion.texto: Mia, de Ecuador, insistió en pagar toda la cena; Tom, de Escocia, creyó que ella ignoraba su oferta de dividir la cuenta y se fue temprano, ofendido. Escribe el mensaje de Mia: nombra el malentendido, aclara tu intención, discúlpate, explica la costumbre, da las gracias por su sinceridad y propón un plan nuevo.
evaluacion.respuesta: Dear Tom, I think there was a misunderstanding at the dinner on Friday, and I would like to clear the air. I did not intend to offend you, and I am very sorry that my insistence on paying may have come across as rude. In my country it is a custom for the person who invites to pay for everybody, and refusing your offer was my way of showing respect, not of ignoring you. I can see now that it may have given the wrong impression, since in Scotland friends usually share the bill. I apologise for not explaining this at the time, and I hope you will give me the benefit of the doubt. Let me clarify something else: I enjoyed the evening very much, and I appreciate your honesty when you told me how you felt. Perhaps we could meet halfway next time: I will choose the restaurant, and you will pay for the dessert. Would you like to have lunch on Saturday? I promise to ask before I reach for the bill. Kind regards, Mia
aceptadas: Hello Tom, I am sorry about the confusion at the dinner. I think we had a misunderstanding, and I never meant to hurt you. Where I come from, the person who invites usually pays for everybody, so when I refused your offer I wanted to show respect, but I see that it may have given the wrong impression and come across as rude to you. I apologise for not explaining that at the moment. Let me clarify: I had a lovely evening, and I want to keep our friendship. I appreciate that you told me how you felt, and I hope you can give me the benefit of the doubt. Perhaps we could go out again on Saturday, and this time we could split the bill so that nobody feels uncomfortable. Would you like that? Thank you for listening.
evaluacion.feedback: Un buen mensaje nombra el malentendido, aclara la intención, se disculpa, explica la costumbre, agradece la sinceridad y propone seguir adelante.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué concluyen Tom y Mia sobre el malentendido?
evaluacion.texto: Tom explained that in Scotland maybe often means no, so he had taken Mia's answer as a refusal. Mia explained that in Ecuador maybe can be a polite way of saying that you are not sure, and that she had never meant to reject him. Both agreed that neither of them had been rude; they had simply been using the same word in different ways.
opciones: That the word means something different in each country and nobody is to blame.
That Tom should have asked more questions about the invitation before he answered.
That Mia should avoid the word maybe whenever she speaks to people from Scotland.
That the misunderstanding came from Tom's lack of good manners at the dinner.
evaluacion.feedback: Los dos reconocen que usaron la misma palabra con valores distintos y que ninguno fue grosero: el malentendido es cultural, no una falta de nadie.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa cada frase de reparación con la palabra que falta.
frases: My reply may have given you the wrong ___.
I hope my words did not come across as ___ to you.
In my country it is a ___ to greet everyone with a hug.
evaluacion.texto: Pistas en español: impresión, grosero, costumbre.
evaluacion.feedback: Impression, rude y custom completan una explicación cultural breve: el efecto, cómo sonó y la costumbre.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «Una disculpa sincera puede ayudarnos a suavizar las cosas.»
evaluacion.respuesta: A sincere apology can help us to smooth things over
evaluacion.feedback: A sincere apology es el sujeto; smooth things over nombra lo que se consigue con ella.

repaso.consigna: Escucha el relato y elige qué actitud muestra Leo al escribir a Mia.
repaso.audio: Leo wrote back to Mia the same evening. He said that he was sorry that his answer had sounded unfriendly, that he had not meant it that way, and that he would like to start again. He added that he would gladly give her the benefit of the doubt, if she would do the same for him.
opciones: Sincere: he accepts part of the blame and asks for trust in return.
Defensive: he apologises only to make Mia admit her own fault.
Resigned: he apologises because he wants to avoid any further contact.
repaso.feedback: Se disculpa porque su respuesta sonó poco amable, pide empezar de nuevo y ofrece confianza a cambio de la misma: actitud sincera, sin defenderse ni rendirse.

repaso.consigna: Aclara en inglés qué quisiste decir con «maybe» y propón empezar de nuevo.
repaso.texto: Un amigo entendió «maybe» como un no. Explica en dos frases qué querías decir, con un suavizante, y propón empezar de nuevo.
repaso.respuesta: I meant that I was not sure yet, but I would love to come. Perhaps we could start again and choose a day that suits us both?
aceptadas: What I meant was that I was not certain, and I would like to come. How about we try again and pick a day that suits us both?
I wanted to say that I was unsure, but I might come. Could we start again and fix a day?
repaso.feedback: Una buena aclaración dice qué querías decir (I meant), mantiene la puerta abierta con un suavizante y propone empezar de nuevo.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Tras la discusión, le envió una nota cálida para suavizar las cosas.»
repaso.texto: After the argument, she sent him a warm note to ___ things over before the weekend.
repaso.feedback: Smooth things over es la expresión para calmar un conflicto y reparar la relación.
